source_refs.note: Topic 15.1 (Methods of Separation of Mixtures), printed page 324.

blocks.text: The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods: filtration, crystallization, simple distillation, fractional distillation and paper chromatography. Each is treated in the following topics.

blocks.caption: The five methods
rows: an insoluble solid from a liquid or solution
a soluble solid from its impurities
a solvent from a solution of a solid
two miscible liquids of different boiling points
soluble substances in a small sample

blocks.prompt: Which technique suits each mixture: petroleum and water; NaCl and NaNO3; activated charcoal and sodium chloride; methanol, ethanol and propanol (Quick Check 15.5b)?
blocks.explanation: Petroleum and water are immiscible liquids: separate with a separating funnel, or distil. NaCl and NaNO3 are two soluble solids: fractional crystallization from water, using their different solubilities. Charcoal and sodium chloride: dissolve the salt in water and filter off the insoluble charcoal, then crystallize. Methanol, ethanol and propanol are miscible liquids with different boiling points: fractional distillation.

items: Physical separation methods: filtration, crystallization, simple distillation, fractional distillation, paper chromatography.
